# RFC-0008: Playbook calls

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Will Eaton

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0008:C-SCOPE] Scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0008c-scope"></a>

A playbook can start a run of another pipeline and use what that run returns. The task that does this is a call. Its target is another Crucible playbook or a pipeline on an external system, first a GitHub Actions workflow started by workflow_dispatch. The target runs as its own run, not as part of the caller's graph. The caller binds the target's inputs from its own task outputs, agent or command alike, including JSON values and files, and receives the target's result as the call's output.

This RFC covers the call task in the workflow DSL, how a pack names and pins its targets, the JSON and file parameter types a target can declare, how the controller dispatches, follows and cancels a target run, and how a client draws one. It does not cover a target that runs inside the caller's run, a call that does not wait for its target, or GitHub credentials other than an App installation.

The parameter types in [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-param-types) extend [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params), and a call task is an engine-owned task under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape). Finalizing this RFC requires amending both.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0008:C-CALL] The call task (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-call"></a>

A playbook or custom workflow MAY declare a call task with call(). A call takes a name, a target, params, and optionally over, budget, depends_on, required, join, stage, and when, with the meanings [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape) and the DSL reference give them on any task. An autoresearch workflow MUST NOT declare one.

target MUST name a target the source's calls block declares ([RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets)). The engine MUST refuse a target that the block does not declare.

params MUST be a dict from the target's declared parameter names to values. A value MUST be one of:

- a literal of the parameter's type;
- param(name), a parameter of the calling workflow;
- producer.field, a field a dependency of the call declares in emits; or
- producer.files[path], a path a dependency of the call declares in emits_files.

A producer MUST be a direct dependency of the call. The engine MUST check every binding against the target's interface in the call lock ([RFC-0008:C-LOCK](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-lock)) at compile time and MUST refuse a source in which a required target parameter is unbound, a name is not a target parameter, a field's declared type does not match the parameter's type, or a file is bound to a parameter that is not a file parameter. A field typed by a schema MUST match only a json parameter, and the parameter's schema, when it has one, MUST be equal to the field's.

over = each(producer.field, max = N) MUST make the call a mapped task: one target run per item, with item available as a value in params. The engine MUST refuse N above 64.

The engine MUST bind every value when the call becomes ready, not at compile time. A value the target refuses, such as one outside a choice set or a pattern, MUST settle the call failing with the refusal as its note before any target run is created and without spend.

A call task's output MUST be the target's result as [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets) defines it, typed by the target's interface, so that dependents, when, and route decisions read it as they read any task's output. The target's result files MUST be staged as the call's declared files under [RFC-0002:C-TASK-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-task-files).

A call MUST settle passing when the target run ends passing, failing when it ends failing, timed out, or cancelled by anything other than its caller, with the target's own note, and cancelled when its caller is cancelled. A call task MUST NOT set complete. A call MUST NOT be a member of a revise loop body or a session.

### [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS] Call targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-targets"></a>

A workflow source MAY declare the targets it calls in a calls block: an assignment to calls that comes before every statement but the params block of [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params), whose value is a dictionary literal from a target name to a dictionary literal built only from dictionaries, lists, strings, numbers, and booleans. The engine and the controller MUST be able to read the block without evaluating the source, MUST refuse a calls assignment anywhere else, and MUST refuse a block that is not such a literal. A target name MUST be unique in the block and every target MUST carry a kind. The engine and the controller MUST refuse a target whose kind they do not implement, and MUST implement the kinds "playbook" and "github_workflow". A manifest MUST NOT declare call targets.

A "playbook" target MUST name a playbook by its registered name, or by a draft the pack's owner may read. A "github_workflow" target MUST name a repo as owner/name, a workflow file path under .github/workflows, a ref that is a branch or tag, and the outputs [RFC-0008:C-GITHUB-WORKFLOW](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-github-workflow) reads.

For each kind the controller MUST implement these operations, and the engine MUST NOT perform any of them itself:

- interface: the target's parameters as a schema of the types [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) and [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-param-types) admit; its result as the fields and files it declares; and its static graph as [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress) shapes it.
- dispatch: start one target run with bound values and return a handle that identifies it on its system.
- progress: the target run's current graph as [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress) shapes it.
- outcome: once the target run ends, its status, its note, its result fields, and its result files.
- cancel: stop the target run.

For a "playbook" target, the interface MUST be the target pack's params block, its workflow result task's emits and emits_files, and its compiled graph; the outcome MUST be its result task's output and files, and its status the run's verdict. A target playbook that declares no result MUST have an empty result.

### [RFC-0008:C-LOCK] Call lock (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-lock"></a>

A pack any of whose workflow sources declares a calls block MUST hold a lock file, calls.lock, at its root. One lock serves every workflow source the manifest names, its variants' included, and two sources that give one target name different targets MUST be refused. For each target name the lock MUST record the target's kind, its pin, and its interface as [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets) defines it, with the digest of the interface. The lock is a pack file, so the pack's digest under [RFC-0002:C-PACK-BASE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-pack-base) covers it, and approving a pack approves its pins.

A pin MUST be one of:

- the digest of a registered playbook's revision;
- a draft's head, which only a draft pack MAY pin, resolved at dispatch to the draft's latest saved version that compiles; or
- for a GitHub workflow, the repo, workflow path and ref, with the commit the ref named when the lock was written.

The controller MUST write the lock when it saves a draft version, and MUST refuse to save, register, or import a pack whose lock is missing, names a target no workflow source declares, omits one a source declares, or records an interface that differs from what the target's interface operation returns for its pin at that time. A crucible command MUST be able to write the lock for a pack in a source repository, given a controller.

The engine MUST check, before compiling anything else, that the lock pins every target its source declares, and MUST compile a call against the lock alone. It MUST NOT contact a target's system to compile, and a compile MUST NOT need the result of another compile.

A pin that moves, a draft head or a git ref, MUST be resolved again at dispatch. The controller MUST refuse to dispatch a target whose interface at dispatch differs from the locked interface, and the call MUST settle failing with a note naming the target and the difference, before any target run is created. A registered pin MUST NOT be resolved again. The controller MUST refuse to register or import a pack whose lock pins a draft head.

### [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES] JSON and file parameters (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-param-types"></a>

A declared parameter MAY have type json or file, in addition to the types [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) lists.

A json parameter's value MUST be a JSON object or array of at most 64 KiB serialized. Its declaration MAY name schema, a path below the pack directory to a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) read under the rules schema_file() follows. A launch MUST be refused when the value does not validate against the schema. A json parameter MUST NOT take choices, choices_from, pattern, or multiline.

A file parameter's value MUST be one file of at most max_bytes, which the declaration MUST set and which MUST NOT exceed 16 MiB. Its declaration MAY name media_type, a list of media types the file must have. The controller MUST store a supplied file as a blob owned by the launch, record its digest and size with the launch, and deliver it beside the pack's tree, never inside it. A file parameter MUST NOT take a default or any value constraint other than max_bytes and media_type.

A command or evaluate task MUST receive a json parameter's value under params as JSON, and a file parameter as an object giving the staged file's path, size, digest, and media type. An agent task MUST receive a json value only inside a region marked as external input, as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) requires, and a file only as a read-only staged input under the same marking; a json value MUST NOT be convertible to plain text, as a string parameter is not.

A launch form MUST take a json parameter as text validated against its schema before submission, and a file parameter as an upload refused above max_bytes. The JSON Schema the engine emits for the params block MUST describe both, with the schema embedded for json.

### [RFC-0008:C-CHILD-RUN] Target runs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-child-run"></a>

When a call becomes ready, the engine MUST ask the controller to dispatch its target, authenticated as its own run, and MUST then wait inside the call's own execution until the controller reports the target run ended. The caller's wall-clock ceiling MUST keep running while it waits.

The controller MUST identify a target run by the calling run, the call task, the mapped instance, and the attempt, and MUST create at most one target run per identity. The engine MUST record the target run's handle in the session log before it waits. A resumed caller MUST attach to the target run its handle names and MUST NOT dispatch a second one, and the target run MUST NOT be cancelled by its caller's interruption alone.

A "playbook" target run MUST be a run of its own, with its own run identity, pack, manifest, sandbox, secrets, and dispatch target, and MUST record the calling run, call task, and instance as its parent. It MUST be launched with the authority of the calling run's launch owner under [RFC-0003:C-DECISION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-decision): the controller MUST refuse to dispatch it, and the call MUST settle failing, when that owner may not launch the target at its pin.

A target run's cost and wall-clock ceilings MUST NOT be drawn from the caller's. A call MAY set budget = budget(cost = ..., wall_clock = ...), and the target run's ceilings MUST then be those values, bounded by what the controller allows a launch of that target. Otherwise they MUST be the ceilings the controller gives a manual launch of the target. The caller's spend MUST NOT include the target run's. For a target that has no cost, wall_clock MUST still bound it: the controller MUST cancel the target run when it is exceeded, and the call MUST settle failing.

Cancelling a calling run MUST cancel every target run it dispatched that has not ended. A target run MUST NOT dispatch a call when it is already the fourth in a chain of calling runs, and the call MUST settle failing.

The controller MUST record, for each target run, the bound values it dispatched with, file digests in place of file contents, so that what left the calling run is auditable.

### [RFC-0008:C-GITHUB-WORKFLOW] GitHub workflow targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-github-workflow"></a>

A "github_workflow" target's interface MUST be read from the workflow file at the pinned commit: its parameters from on.workflow_dispatch.inputs, where string, choice, and environment inputs are string parameters, a boolean input is a boolean parameter, and a number input is a number parameter; and its static graph from its jobs and their needs. Its result MUST be the outputs the manifest entry declares: the name of an artifact the workflow uploads, the fields of a JSON object at result.json in that artifact, and the paths of further files in it. The controller MUST refuse a workflow file that has no workflow_dispatch trigger or more inputs than GitHub accepts.

A json parameter of a call MUST be bound to a string input and sent as its serialized JSON. A file parameter MUST NOT be bound to a GitHub workflow input, and the engine MUST refuse a lock or source that does.

The controller MUST dispatch with the token of the GitHub App installation on the target repository, and MUST refuse a target whose repository the App is not installed on or whose installation lacks actions write permission. It MUST dispatch on the pinned ref, MUST request the created run's details, and MUST use the run identifier GitHub returns as the handle. It MUST NOT find the run by searching recent runs. It MUST record the head commit the run ran on.

The controller SHOULD learn progress from verified workflow_run and workflow_job deliveries under [RFC-0003:C-WEBHOOK-DELIVERY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-webhook-delivery) and MUST also poll the run and its jobs, so that a lost delivery delays the outcome but cannot lose it.

A completed run's conclusion MUST map as follows: success to passing; failure, timed_out, startup_failure, action_required, and stale to failing; cancelled to failing unless the caller cancelled it; skipped and neutral to passing with an empty result. A passing run whose declared artifact or result.json is missing, unreadable, or does not match the declared fields MUST settle the call failing with a note naming what is missing.

### [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS] Target progress (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-progress"></a>

For every target kind, the controller MUST describe a target's static graph and a target run's progress in one shape: a list of nodes and a list of edges between them. A node MUST carry an identifier unique within the graph, a label, and a status; and MAY carry a group, start and end times, a kind-specific detail, and a link. The status MUST be one of the task statuses a Crucible run's graph uses, so that one renderer draws every kind, and each kind MUST state its mapping.

For a "playbook" target, nodes MUST be the target run's tasks and their mapped instances, with the run's own statuses, and a node's link MUST name the target run and task. For a "github_workflow" target, nodes MUST be its jobs, with matrix legs of one job in one group and edges from needs; a node's detail MUST list the job's steps with their status and times, and its link MUST be the job's page on GitHub. Before dispatch, the static graph from the lock MUST be served with every node pending.

The controller MUST serve the progress of every target run a run dispatched to whoever may read the calling run, and MUST NOT serve to a reader of the calling run anything else of a playbook target run that the reader may not read under [RFC-0003:C-READ-SCOPING](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-read-scoping): such a node MUST show its label and status and no link. The controller MUST bound a progress graph at 512 nodes and say how many it left out.

### [RFC-0008:C-VIEW] Drawing calls (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-view"></a>

A client that draws a run's graph MUST draw a call task as a node distinct from other task kinds, labelled with its alias and target kind, and MUST let a reader expand it into the target's graph from [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress), drawn inside a frame attached to the call's place in the caller's graph. A mapped call MUST draw one frame per instance and fold them as other mapped tasks fold. An edge into a call SHOULD be labelled with the parameter it binds.

From an expanded call, a reader MUST be able to open a node's link: a node of a playbook target opens that task in the target run, and a node of an external target opens its page outside the client. The call node MUST also open the target run as a whole. A client showing a playbook run that a call dispatched MUST show the calling run and call task and open them, so that a reader can move from caller to target and back.

A client that lists runs SHOULD list a run a call dispatched under the run that called it rather than beside it.

A client that previews a pack's graph before launch MUST draw each call's static graph from the lock.
